What is the equation of the parabola shown above?

feedback.problem: Find the equation of the downward-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(0,4)$ and which passes through the point $(4,-8).$
feedback.worked_solution:
For any upward or downward-opening parabola with its vertex at $(h,k),$ the general standard equation is given by

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k).
$$

Here, the vertex has coordinates $(h,k)=(0,4).$ Substituting these into the general standard equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-0)^{2} & =4p(y-4) \\ {x}^{2} & =4p(y-4).\end{aligned}
$$

We are left to find the value of $p.$ We know that the given parabola also passes through the point $(4,-8),$ so we can substitute $x=4$ and $y=-8$ into the standard equation and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & =4p(y-4) \\ {4}^{2} & =4p(-8-4) \\ 16 & =-48p \\ p & =-\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & =4p(y-4) \\ {x}^{2} & =4(-\frac{1}{3})(y-4) \\ {x}^{2} & =-\frac{4}{3}(y-4).\end{aligned}
$$
